segmentNote: Mostly a builder: construction is 96% of revenue. Data centres were the biggest source of new work in 2025 (AR p.13, p.248).

how.title: How Sunway Construction makes money
how.text: Revenue = construction work done for clients, billed as each project progresses + sales of precast concrete parts

story.scale_label: order book: work won but not yet built
story.debt_label: net cash, more cash than borrowings

debt.label: net cash, more cash than borrowings

items.label: Construction costs
items.tip: Subcontractors, materials, site staff and equipment for projects.

items.label: Administrative expenses
items.tip: Head office, staff bonuses and share options, IT and tender costs.

items.label: Finance costs
items.tip: Interest on short-term trade financing and loans.

items.label: Partners' share of profit
items.tip: Profit belonging to joint-venture partners in subsidiaries.

items.label: Impairments and other costs
items.tip: Allowances for customers who may not pay, and other costs.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: Plus about RM2.62 per RM100 of revenue from interest on its cash, other income and joint ventures.

fiveYear.note: New orders won (RM billion): 2021 1.5 · 2022 2.6 · 2023 2.5 · 2024 4.2 · 2025 5.2. Profit nearly doubled in 2025 on data-centre work.

rows.name: Construction
rows.tip: Building data centres, factories, warehouses, buildings and infrastructure in Malaysia, plus public housing in Singapore.

rows.name: Precast concrete
rows.tip: Making precast concrete parts in factories, mainly for Singapore public housing.

segments.note: Revenue from outside customers; profit attributable to shareholders by segment (AR p.248).

assets.label: Owed by Sunway companies and joint ventures

liabilities.label: Owed to Sunway companies and joint ventures

balance.note: A light, cash-rich builder: RM2.0bn of cash against RM0.3bn of borrowings. Most of its funding comes from what it owes subcontractors and suppliers (RM3.0bn), which is normal for contractors.

cash.wfNote: Cash from operations reached RM1.6bn, helped by RM793m more owed to subcontractors and suppliers. The 23 sen special dividend declared in November was mostly paid after year-end.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM10.3 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2025 profit)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM29 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: Includes a one-off 23 sen special dividend. Without it, the regular dividends of 27.5 sen give about 3.5%.

metrics.label: Payout ratio FY2025
metrics.plain: Paid out more than the year's profit because of the special dividend; regular payouts were 53-60% in earlier years (AR p.15).

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 13.2 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity FY2025
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM44 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2025
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM6.78.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Net cash
metrics.plain: Cash and investments minus borrowings: RM1,700 million. Positive means no net debt.

metrics.label: Free cash flow FY2025
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM1,575 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: EV / EBITDA
metrics.plain: A price tag that includes debt: about 14.7 times its yearly cash earnings before interest and tax.

drivers.evidence: RM2.9bn of data centre orders in 2025; RM13-14bn of data-centre contracts expected to progress by mid-2026 (AR p.13, p.17)
drivers.why: The main source of new work and profit growth.

drivers.evidence: RM5.2bn of new orders in 2025, the highest since listing (AR p.13)
drivers.why: Keeps revenue growing for the next two years.

drivers.evidence: RM5.7bn order book is about one year of revenue (AR p.15)
drivers.why: SunCon must keep winning jobs to sustain growth.

drivers.evidence: RM1.9bn of orders from in-house Sunway developments (AR p.13)
drivers.why: Steady work from its parent, but tied to Sunway's property plans.

drivers.evidence: Continued work on Singapore's Build-To-Order programme (AR p.14, p.37)
drivers.why: Government-backed demand for precast and building work.

drivers.evidence: Gross margin rose from 13.6% to 15.4% (AR p.237)
drivers.why: Data centre jobs and execution lifted profitability.

drivers.evidence: Higher electricity tariffs, wage adjustments and material price swings (AR p.13)
drivers.why: Fixed-price contracts lose margin when costs rise.

drivers.evidence: RM30m net impairment on receivables vs a RM10m write-back in 2024 (AR p.237)
drivers.why: Shows some customers are slower to pay.

drivers.evidence: RM2.0bn cash vs RM0.3bn borrowings at end-2025 (AR p.238-239)
drivers.why: Strong balance sheet to fund growth and dividends.

drivers.evidence: 50.5 sen including a 23 sen special; payout 184% of profit (AR p.15)
drivers.why: Generous, but the special part may not repeat.

drivers.evidence: About 29 times FY2025 profit at RM7.81 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: The price assumes the data-centre wave continues.

outlook.text: About RM13-14bn of data-centre construction contracts are expected to progress towards delivery by mid-2026 (AR p.17).
Industrial, logistics and selected public projects are expected to support construction demand (AR p.17).
Malaysia's growth in 2026 is expected to be moderate but resilient (AR p.17).
Cost pressures from electricity tariffs, wages and materials, and global uncertainty (AR p.13, p.17).

outlookOverall.text: Management expects a steady pipeline of data-centre, industrial and infrastructure work in 2026 (AR p.17).
